-37.29575,143.78288: Former Clunes Free Library. The Mechanics Library Institution was established in 1862 and reformed as the Free Library in 1874. The building, designed by Sheridan and built by Stone & Barwell, was opened in 1882. The building is notable for its double gable facade and render work.

-37.42882,143.89345: Former Creswick Gold Office is registered by Heritage Council Victoria. Built in 1858, this relic of a once-thriving goldmining town is one of the earliest permanent public offices for the administration of mining activities in Victoria. Design: Public Works Department. Architect: C. J. Ross.
-37.46099,143.97913: Dean Hall & Mechanics Institute. Established on this site in 1891. The Mechanics' Institute movement began in British urban industrial centres in the early 1800s. A "mechanic" was a person applying skills and technology. During the 19th century, most towns in Victoria established a Mechanics' Institute or Athenaeum with a library and meeting hall. Common objects were the "spread of useful knowledge" and provision for "rational recreation" in the community. This plaque, No 17 in the MIV series, acknowledges the vision and dedicated contribution of supporters of Dean and district who have ensured the continuity of Dean Hall and Mechanics Institute as a focal point for the community for successive generations. Dedicated in 2006 in the 115th Anniversary year to celebrate the refurbishment of the historic building.
